correctness.rationale: The Fibonacci-word concatenation W_{k+2}=W_kW_{k-1}W_k and an inductive two-letter near-commutation prove the first disagreement is exactly F_{k+1}-2. For k>=4 its canonical encoding has k-1 digits. A two-state last-digit DFAO, a four-state validity DFA, and any s-state shifted DFAO form a discrepancy DFA of at most 8s states. Its shortest accepted word has length k-1, forcing at least k states. Independent finite morphic and Zeckendorf computations successfully check k=4..20 and 25,000 sequence digits; the finite tests are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact first-disagreement location for Fibonacci shifts is combined with a canonical-language discrepancy automaton to force a new explicit MSD-first lower bound linear in the Fibonacci index. The closest primary article proves a logarithmic upper bound for MSD-first machines, and exact minimal state counts only for LSD-first. The companion automata results also provide upper bounds, not this lower bound. Available prior-claim and indexed-literature comparisons did not identify this statement; undiscovered equivalents remain possible.
